questiontext.text: In Pipes and Filters, how does data move through the system?

answer.text: Through a pipeline of filters connected by pipes

feedback.text: Correct — each filter transforms and passes the stream on.

answer.text: By broadcasting to all components at once

feedback.text: That resembles pub-sub, not a pipeline.
Pipes and filters decompose processing into stages.

answer.text: By storing everything in one shared variable

feedback.text: Not how the pattern works.

generalfeedback.text: Data flows through a chain of filters; pipes connect them, and each filter transforms the stream and passes it to the next.

answer.text: Transforms its input stream and passes the result on

feedback.text: Correct — a filter is an independent transformation stage.
Filters transform streams; they are not the datastore.

answer.text: Coordinates all other filters as a controller

feedback.text: Filters are independent; there is no central coordinator.
That is Observer/pub-sub behavior.

generalfeedback.text: A filter reads from its input pipe, transforms the data, and writes to its output pipe, independent of neighboring filters.

questiontext.text: Which everyday system is a classic example of pipes and filters?

feedback.text: Correct — each command is a filter joined by pipes.
An index is a data structure, not a pipeline.
That is event handling, not a filter chain.
Unrelated to the pattern.

generalfeedback.text: Unix pipelines are the archetypal pipes-and-filters system: each command transforms the stream and pipes it onward.

answer.text: They are composable and reusable in different pipelines

feedback.text: Correct — filters can be recombined freely.

answer.text: They force all stages into one class

feedback.text: The opposite — filters are separate stages.
Filters communicate via pipes, not shared globals.

answer.text: They must all run before any data flows

feedback.text: Streaming lets data flow through incrementally.

generalfeedback.text: Because filters are independent and share a stream interface, they can be composed and reused across pipelines.

questiontext.text: Which statements about pipes and filters are true? (select all that apply)

feedback.text: Yes.

answer.text: Pipes connect the output of one filter to the input of the next

feedback.text: Yes.

answer.text: A central controller must orchestrate every filter

feedback.text: No — filters run independently along the pipeline.

answer.text: Filters must share mutable global state to communicate

feedback.text: No — they communicate through pipes.

generalfeedback.text: Pipes and filters compose independent transformation stages connected by pipes, with no central coordinator or shared global state.

questiontext.text: In pipes and filters, each filter transforms the data stream and passes it on, and filters can be recombined.

feedback.text: Correct — independence makes filters reusable and composable.
Transform-and-pass-on with composability is the essence of the pattern.

questiontext.text: Pipes and filters require a central controller that directly manages the state of every filter.

feedback.text: No — filters are independent stages with no central manager.
Correct — filters run independently, connected only by pipes.

questiontext.text: In this style, each independent stage that transforms the data stream is called a ______. (one word, English)

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.
Accepted — pipes connect the filters.
